title: SEA@DEN-card-REFUSED
universal_lens: The fixture refusal operator defines a strict boundary condition on the analytical manifold. When an input tuple lacks a valid mapping to the confirmed temporal slate, the system enforces a zero-measure projection, preventing the generation of fictitious analytical states.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, this maps to a hard conformal prediction failure. If the requested matchup falls outside the empirical training distribution of the active period, the conformal interval collapses to null, triggering a definitive rejection of any probabilistic inference.
gse_mapping: For GSE, the situational reasoning engine halts state transitions upon detecting a non-existent game node. The transition matrix yields a singular identity block, enforcing a static 'REFUSED' state rather than hallucinating dynamic opponent interactions.

primitives.name: Fixture Existence Predicate
primitives.verbatim_quote: # SEA@DEN - FIXTURE NOT CONFIRMED (card REFUSED) **This matchup is not a game on the real 411 slate.** The engine does not emit an analyst card for a fixture it cannot confirm.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S: Set of confirmed fixtures (dimensionless); x: Input matchup tuple; I_S(x): Indicator function returning 1 if x \in S, else 0.
primitives.assumptions: The operational slate S is strictly finite and fully enumerated prior to inference.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if the scheduling authority introduces late-stage slate mutations without updating the foundational existence predicate.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a domain validity check in measure theory, ensuring the integrand is only evaluated over the defined support set.
layer2.telemetry: Boolean flag indicating whether the requested matchup exists in the canonical schedule database.

primitives.name: Fiction Suppression Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: A card here would be fiction that reads as analysis.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: F: Space of fictional outputs; A: Space of valid analytical outputs; K: Suppression kernel mapping F -> \emptyset.
primitives.assumptions: Any output generated from an invalid input inherently belongs to the space of fiction F.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the system's definition of 'analysis' becomes degenerate enough to accept hallucinated data as empirical truth.

layer2.mapping: Acts as a regularization term with infinite penalty weight for out-of-distribution inputs, forcing the loss function to reject the sample entirely.
layer2.telemetry: Zero-count metric for emitted cards when the existence predicate evaluates to false.

primitives.name: Temporal Slate Anchor
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Why this card was refused - FIXTURE NOT ON SLATE: SEA@DEN is not a game in Week 5, 2026 (period 411).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: t: Temporal period identifier (e.g., 411); M: Matchup entity; \delta_{t}(M): Kronecker delta verifying M is scheduled at t.
primitives.assumptions: Time is discretized into immutable periods where the set of matchups is fixed and known.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities arise during off-season projections or hypothetical simulations where the temporal anchor is undefined.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to the time-step validation layer in GSE, ensuring state vectors are only constructed for valid temporal indices.
layer2.telemetry: Discrepancy count between requested period ID and the actual period ID hosting the matchup.

This zero-measure event triggers the Fiction Suppression Kernel. This rigorous adherence to the confirmed slate ensures the epistemic integrity of all downstream Bayesian inferences.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This logic traces back to the foundational axioms of formal logic and database consistency, specifically the closed-world assumption used in relational algebra. Historically, early quantitative models suffered from 'garbage-in, garbage-out' hallucinations when forced to interpolate across non-existent events. The development of hard constraint solvers in operations research provided the blueprint for treating missing fixtures not as missing data to be imputed, but as structural impossibilities requiring immediate termination of the inference pipeline.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The engine models the user as an agent potentially suffering from a memory lapse regarding the official schedule or intentionally probing the system's boundaries with hypothetical matchups. By refusing the card and explicitly stating 'this is fiction,' the system adopts a pedagogical stance. It assumes the user desires genuine analytical insight rather than plausible-sounding nonsense. The counter-strategy involves guiding the user back to the true state space by providing the actual opponents, thereby aligning the user's intent with the empirical reality of the league's schedule.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The cross-layer veto is activated when the GSI probabilistic layer attempts to draw priors for a non-existent game. The GSE situational layer intercepts this request via the existence predicate. If the GSI layer were allowed to proceed, it would introduce severe anti-collinearity issues, as the generated features would have no grounding in observable reality. The veto condition is absolute: if the temporal slate anchor fails, all higher-order feature extractions and conformal inference routines are immediately suspended, ensuring zero leakage of synthetic data into the sovereign primitives.
